These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1. Being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.5,29,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant as well as the Insurance Company are in appeals.
The occurrence of the accident is not in dispute and the liability of the insurer to pay compensation is also not in dispute.

3. The insurer, however, contends that as per the deposition of the claimant himself, he had continued his earlier job and therefore, the question of awarding any sums towards 'loss of future income' would be incorrect.
4. The claimant, on the other hand, contends that he was a Site Engineer and as a result of his disability, he is unable to function effectively.

In my view, since there is no evidence that the income of the claimant has diminished as a result of the accident, the award Rs.3,76,320/- towards 'loss of future income' awarded by the Tribunal cannot be sustained.
However, it is noticed that the claimant has suffered a fracture of both the bones of his left leg.

In that view the matter, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.1,00,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities'.

The sum of Rs.31,949/- awarded towards 'medical expenses' is affirmed.
6. Similarly, the sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded towards 'nourishment and attendant charges' and conveyance' is also just proper and is affirmed.
7. It is noticed that the Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards 'loss of income during the laid-up period'.

Since the claimant has suffered fracture of both the bones of his left leg, it would be appropriate to take the laid-up period as three months and award a sum of Rs.60,000/-
(Rs.20,000*3 months) towards 'loss of income during laid- up period'.
8. The sum of Rs.30,000/- awarded towards 'future medical expenses' is also affirmed.

9. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

laid-up period Conveyance, food, 20,000 20,000 6
. nourishment, attendant charges 7.
Loss of amenities in life 20,000 1,00,000 Total 5,28,269 3,41,949 10.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.3,41,949/- as against Rs.5,28,269/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
11. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
